\chapter{Chapter08 — Biased Threshold Phenomena}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter08.BiasedThresholdPhenomena}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous biased sign distribution]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b004
}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The heterogeneous biased sign distribution on sign vectors of
length $n$ is the product probability distribution whose coordinate $i$ has the biased
sign distribution with parameter $p_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous biased monomial]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p221-b002}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedStandardizedSign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ assign a real parameter to each of the $n$
coordinates, let $S$ be a set of coordinates, and let $x$ be a sign vector. The
heterogeneous biased monomial indexed by $S$ is the product, over coordinates in $S$, of
the standardized biased sign at that coordinate, evaluated at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous biased Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p221-b002}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let each coordinate parameter $p_i$ lie in $(0,1)$, let $f$
be a real-valued function on sign vectors of length $n$, and let $S$ be a set of
coordinates. The heterogeneous biased Fourier coefficient indexed by $S$ is the
expectation, under the product distribution with coordinate parameters $p_i$, of $f(x)$
times the heterogeneous biased monomial indexed by $S$, evaluated at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cube partial derivative]
\lean{FABL.cubePartialDerivativeAt}
\label{FABL.cubePartialDerivativeAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff}
Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let
$\mu:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb R$. Define the partial derivative associated with $S$,
evaluated at $\mu$, by summing over all coordinate sets $T$ containing $S$: the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $T$ multiplied by the product of $\mu_i$ over $i\in T\setminus S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous basis partial derivative]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBasisPartialDerivativeAt}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBasisPartialDerivativeAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasSigma, FABL.cubePartialDerivativeAt}
Let $p$ assign a real parameter to each of the $n$ coordinates, let
$f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $S$ be a set of coordinates, and let $x$ assign a real
number to each coordinate. The heterogeneous-basis partial derivative at $x$ is the cube
partial derivative associated with $S$ at $x$, multiplied by the product over $i\in S$
of the bias scale factor at $p_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sign times standardized sign]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF_sign_mul_standardized}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF_sign_mul_standardized}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.biasMean, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasSigma_pos, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedStandardizedSign_sq, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $0<p<1$, and choose a sign $X\in\{-1,1\}$ according to the probability distribution
with mean $1-2p$. Write $\sigma=\sqrt{4p(1-p)}$ and $Z=(X-(1-2p))/\sigma$. Then the
expected value of $XZ$ is $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product of ordinary and biased monomials]
\lean{FABL.monomial_mul_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\label{FABL.monomial_mul_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ assign a real parameter to each of the $n$
coordinates, let $T$ and $S$ be subsets of the coordinate indices, and let $x$ be a
vector of $n$ signs. For each coordinate $i$, write
$m_i=(x_i-(1-2p_i))/\sqrt{4p_i(1-p_i)}$. The ordinary monomial on $T$ times the monomial
formed from these standardized signs on $S$ equals $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} (\mathbf{1}_{i\in
T}x_i+\mathbf{1}_{i\notin T})(\mathbf{1}_{i\in S}m_i+\mathbf{1}_{i\notin S})$, where
each indicator is $1$ when its condition holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of mixed biased monomials]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_monomial_mul_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_monomial_mul_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.biasMean, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_mul_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF_signValue, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF_sign_mul_standardized, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one, FABL.pmfExpectation_independentProductPMF_prod, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $S,T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For independent random
signs whose coordinate $i$ has mean $1-2p_i$, the expectation of the ordinary sign
monomial on $T$ times the monomial formed on $S$ from signs centered by their respective
means and divided by their standard deviations is $\left(\prod_{i\in
S}2\sqrt{p_i(1-p_i)}\right)\left(\prod_{i\in T\setminus S}(1-2p_i)\right)$ when
$S\subseteq T$, and is $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S$ be a set of
coordinates. The Fourier coefficient of $f$ against the product of the standardized
biased signs on $S$ equals the product of their standard deviations times the sum, over
all coordinate sets $T\supseteq S$, of the ordinary Fourier coefficient on $T$ weighted
by $\prod_{i\in T\setminus S}(1-2p_i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute deviation of a standardized biased sign]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_biasedStandardizedSign}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_biasedStandardizedSign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasSigma_pos, FABL.biasSigma_sq, FABL.biasVarianceScale, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.biasedStandardizedSign_neg_one_eq, FABL.biasedStandardizedSign_one_eq, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $0<p<1$, and choose a random sign $X\in\{-1,1\}$ with probabilities
$\mathbb{P}(X=1)=1-p$ and $\mathbb{P}(X=-1)=p$. Its mean is $1-2p$ and its standard
deviation is $\sigma=\sqrt{4p(1-p)}$; the expected absolute value of $(X-(1-2p))/\sigma$
is $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute moment of a heterogeneous biased monomial]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_biasedStandardizedSign, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one, FABL.pmfExpectation_independentProductPMF_prod}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, choose parameters $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be
independent random signs with $\mathbb{P}(X_i=1)=1-p_i$ and $\mathbb{P}(X_i=-1)=p_i$,
and set $\sigma_i=\sqrt{4p_i(1-p_i)}$. Then
\[\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\prod_{i\in S}\frac{X_i-(1-2p_i)}{\sigma_i}\right|\right]=\prod_{i\in S}\sigma_i.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Biased Fourier coefficient bound]
\lean{FABL.abs_heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff_le}
\label{FABL.abs_heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasSigma, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_abs_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p_i\\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate $i$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
sign cube, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The absolute value of the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ under the independent biased sign distribution, using the
standardized coordinate monomials, is at most $\\left(\\prod_{i\\in
S}\\sqrt{4p_i(1-p_i)}\\right)\\|f\\|_\\infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected biased-cube monomial]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_monomial}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_monomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasMean, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedMonomial, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_monomial_mul_heterogeneousBiasedMonomial}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p=(p_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ satisfy $0<p_i<1$ for
every coordinate, and let $S\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. Under the independent product
distribution with coordinate parameters $p$, the expectation of the sign monomial
indexed by $S$ is $\prod_{i\in S}(1-2p_i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected discrete derivative under biased signs]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasMean, FABL.cubePartialDerivativeAt, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_eq_fourier_sum, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation_sum}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p=(p_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ satisfy $0<p_i<1$ for
every coordinate, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate
$i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. Under the independent product distribution whose coordinate signs
have the biases specified by $p$, the expectation of the discrete derivative of $f$ in
coordinate $i$ equals the cube partial derivative of $f$ at the singleton $\{i\}$,
evaluated with coordinate means $1-2p_j$: $\mathbb{E}[D_i
f]=\partial_{\{i\}}f\bigl((1-2p_j)_j\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous biased influence]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b002
}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.coordinateConditionalVariance, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let each coordinate parameter $p_i$ lie in $(0,1)$, let $f$
be a real-valued function on sign vectors of length $n$, and fix a coordinate $i$. The
heterogeneous biased influence at $i$ is the expectation, under the product distribution
with coordinate parameters $p_j$, of the conditional variance of $f$ in coordinate $i$,
where that coordinate has its biased sign distribution with parameter $p_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous biased flip probability]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFlipProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b002}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFlipProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. For a coordinate $i$, the
heterogeneous biased flip probability of $f$ at $i$ is the probability, under the
product distribution on sign vectors whose coordinate signs have biases specified by
$p$, that flipping coordinate $i$ changes the value of $f$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.thresholdSignMeasurableSingletonClass}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b003}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone in the
coordinatewise order, and choose a coordinate $i$ and an input $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The
indicator that changing coordinate $i$ of $x$ changes the value of $f$ equals the
discrete derivative $\bigl(f(x_{i\leftarrow 1})-f(x_{i\leftarrow -1})\bigr)/2$, where
$x_{i\leftarrow b}$ denotes $x$ with coordinate $i$ set to $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence and singleton Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence_eq_sigma_mul_singletonCoeff_of_monotone}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b003
}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence_eq_sigma_mul_singletonCoeff_of_monotone}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFlipProbability, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedFourierCoeff_eq_prod_sigma_mul_partialDerivative, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence_eq_sigma_sq_mul_flipProbability, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pivotalIndicator_eq_discreteDerivative_of_monotone, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let each coordinate bias $p_i$ lie in $(0,1)$, and let
$f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be monotone. For every coordinate $i$, its influence under the
product distribution with coordinate biases $(p_i)$ equals the standard deviation of the
biased sign at $i$ times the biased Fourier coefficient of the real-valued sign function
$f$ on the singleton set $\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous biased total influence]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedTotalInfluence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b002
}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedTotalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p=(p_i)_{i=0}^{n-1}$ be a sequence of real numbers
with $0<p_i<1$ for every $i$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube
$\\{-1,1\}^n$. The heterogeneous biased total influence of $f$ at bias vector $p$ is the
sum, over all coordinates $i$, of the heterogeneous biased influence of $f$ in
coordinate $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Biased sign mass]
\lean{FABL.biasedSignMass}
\label{FABL.biasedSignMass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a real parameter $p$ and a sign $b$, the biased sign mass is $1-p$ when $b=1$, and
$p$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of biased sign mass]
\lean{FABL.biasedSignMass_pos}
\label{FABL.biasedSignMass_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.biasedSignMass}
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $p$ with $0<p<1$ and every sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$, the biased sign
mass at $b$ is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator formula for signs]
\lean{FABL.sign_eq_indicator_formula}
\label{FABL.sign_eq_indicator_formula}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For any two signs $b,x\in\{-1,1\}$, the indicator that $x=b$ is $\frac{1+bx}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monomial after deleting a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.monomial_erase_mul_coordinate}
\label{FABL.monomial_erase_mul_coordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $S$ be a finite set of coordinates, let $i\in S$, and let $x$ be a sign assignment.
The monomial on $S$ with coordinate $i$ deleted, multiplied by the sign at $i$, equals
the monomial on $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative and coordinate sign correlation]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative_mul_sign}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative_mul_sign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasMean, FABL.cubePartialDerivativeAt, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_eq_fourier_sum, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_erase_mul_coordinate, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative, FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation_sum, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p=(p_j)_{j\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ satisfy $0<p_j<1$ for
every coordinate, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$.
Under the independent product distribution with coordinate parameters $p$, the
expectation of the product of the discrete derivative $D_i f$ and the $i$th coordinate
sign equals $(1-2p_i)$ times the expectation of $D_i f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative expectation on a biased sign cube]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_discreteDerivative_mul_coordinateIndicator}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_discreteDerivative_mul_coordinateIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.biasMean, FABL.biasedSignMass, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF_discreteDerivative_mul_sign, FABL.signValue, FABL.sign_eq_indicator_formula}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and choose
a sign vector $X\in\{-1,1\}^n$ with independent coordinates, where
$\mathbb{P}(X_i=1)=1-p_i$ and $\mathbb{P}(X_i=-1)=p_i$. For any real-valued function $f$
on the sign cube, coordinate $i$, and sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$, the expectation of its
discrete derivative in coordinate $i$ times the indicator of $X_i=b$ equals the
probability of that sign times the expectation of the derivative; that probability is
$1-p_i$ if $b=1$ and $p_i$ if $b=-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Output pivotality]
\lean{FABL.IsOutputPivotal}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p046-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b006
}
\label{FABL.IsOutputPivotal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$b\in\{\pm1\}$, let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Say that $i$ is
output-pivotal for $f$ at $x$ with output $b$ when $f(x)=b$ and coordinate $i$ is
pivotal for $f$ at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Output at a pivotal coordinate]
\lean{FABL.monotone_output_eq_coordinate_of_isPivotal}
\label{FABL.monotone_output_eq_coordinate_of_isPivotal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.isPivotal_iff_setCoordinate_ne, FABL.neg_one_le_sign, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate_apply_of_ne, FABL.setCoordinate_apply_self, FABL.setCoordinate_eq_self, FABL.sign_eq_neg_one_of_le_neg_one, FABL.sign_eq_one_of_one_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, and let $i$ be a coordinate and $x$ an input.
If flipping coordinate $i$ changes the value of $f$, then $f(x)=x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output pivotality for monotone functions]
\lean{FABL.isOutputPivotal_iff_coordinate_eq_of_monotone}
\label{FABL.isOutputPivotal_iff_coordinate_eq_of_monotone}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.Sign, FABL.monotone_output_eq_coordinate_of_isPivotal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f\colon\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be monotone, let $b\in\{−1,1\}$, and let $i$ be a
coordinate and $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The output of $f$ at $x$ equals $b$ and changing
coordinate $i$ changes the output if and only if $x_i=b$ and changing coordinate $i$
changes the output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Heterogeneous output pivotal probability]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b006}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.Sign, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let
$f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and choose an output sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$ and coordinate $i$.
The heterogeneous output pivotal probability of $f$ at $b$ in coordinate $i$ is the
probability, under the product distribution on sign vectors whose coordinate $j$ is
biased according to $p_j$, that changing coordinate $i$ makes $f$ output $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Biased output pivotal probability]
\lean{FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b006}
\label{FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.Sign, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.productMean}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean
function, let $b\in\{\pm1\}$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The biased output pivotal
probability of $f$ for output $b$ at coordinate $i$ is the probability, when the input
coordinates are independently drawn from the $p$-biased sign distribution, that changing
coordinate $i$ can change the output from $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Output pivotal probability under constant bias]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability_const}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign, FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability, FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $p\in(0,1)$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, choose an
output sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$, and choose a coordinate $i$. When every coordinate has bias
$p$, the probability that $f$ outputs $b$ and changing coordinate $i$ changes the
output, under the heterogeneous product distribution, equals the corresponding
probability under the product distribution with common bias $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence under constant bias]
\lean{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence_const}
\label{FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productInfluence_eq_expect_coordinateConditionalVariance, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedSiteFourierBasis, FABL.heterogeneousBiasedInfluence, FABL.productInfluence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $p\in(0,1)$, $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a
coordinate. When every coordinate has bias $p$, the expected conditional variance of $f$
at coordinate $i$ under the heterogeneous product distribution equals the
product-measure influence at coordinate $i$ for the common biased sign distribution.
\end{theorem}

Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, let
$b\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Then the squared bias standard deviation
times the probability that the output is $b$ and coordinate $i$ is pivotal equals the
biased mass of $b$ times the influence of coordinate $i$:
$\sigma(p)^2\,\Pr_p[f(x)=b\text{ and }i\text{ is pivotal at
}x]=\mu_p(b)\,\operatorname{Inf}_{p,i}(f)$.
\end{theorem}

Let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f$ be a monotone function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to
the two signs, and let $i$ be a coordinate. Under the product distribution with bias
parameter $p$, the influence of the real-valued sign representation of $f$ at $i$ equals
$4(1-p)$ times the probability that $f$ outputs $-1$ and changing coordinate $i$ changes
its output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence and positive-output pivotal probability]
\lean{FABL.productInfluence_eq_four_mul_bias_mul_onePivotalProbability_of_monotone}
\label{FABL.productInfluence_eq_four_mul_bias_mul_onePivotalProbability_of_monotone}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasSigma_sq, FABL.biasVarianceScale, FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability, FABL.biasedSignMass, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.sigma_sq_mul_biasedOutputPivotalProbability_eq_mass_mul_influence_of_monotone}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f$ be a monotone function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to
the two signs, and let $i$ be a coordinate. Under the product distribution with bias
parameter $p$, the influence of the real-valued sign representation of $f$ at $i$ equals
$4p$ times the probability that $f$ outputs $+1$ and changing coordinate $i$ changes its
output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dictator pivotal probability]
\lean{FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability_dictator_one_quarter}
\label{FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability_dictator_one_quarter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability, FABL.biasedSignMass, FABL.dictator, FABL.dictator_monotone, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_apply, FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability_const, FABL.heterogeneousOutputPivotalProbability_eq_mass_mul_derivativeMean_of_monotone, FABL.pmfExpectation_const}
\difficulty{4}
For the dictator function on the one-dimensional sign cube, the probability under the
product distribution with each coordinate equal to $-1$ with probability $1/4$ that its
output is $-1$ and flipping its sole coordinate changes the output is exactly $1/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence of a one-coordinate dictator]
\lean{FABL.productInfluence_dictator_one_quarter}
\label{FABL.productInfluence_dictator_one_quarter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasSigma_sq, FABL.biasVarianceScale, FABL.biasedFlipProbability, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.dictator, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productInfluence_biased_eq_sigma_sq_mul_flipProbability, FABL.productMean, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
On the one-dimensional sign cube, the influence of the function that returns its sole
input coordinate, under the product distribution with bias parameter $1/4$, is $3/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure of the pivotal probability formula]
\lean{FABL.printed_outputPivotal_probability_formula_false}
\label{FABL.printed_outputPivotal_probability_formula_false}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability, FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability_dictator_one_quarter, FABL.biasedSignMass, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.dictator, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productInfluence_dictator_one_quarter}
\difficulty{3}
On the one-dimensional sign cube, let $f(x)=x$, take bias parameter $p=1/4$, output sign
$-1$, and coordinate $1$. Under the product distribution with probabilities $3/4$ for
$+1$ and $1/4$ for $-1$, the probability that $f(x)=-1$ and flipping the coordinate
changes the output is not equal to the mass of $-1$ times the squared $L^2$ distance of
$f$ from its projection onto functions independent of that coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Output pivotal count]
\lean{FABL.outputPivotalCount}
\label{FABL.outputPivotalCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.Sign}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $b$ be a
sign and $x$ a point of the cube. The output pivotal count is the number of coordinates
that are output pivotal for $f$, with respect to $b$ at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator sum for output-pivotal coordinates]
\lean{FABL.outputPivotalCount_cast}
\label{FABL.outputPivotalCount_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.Sign, FABL.outputPivotalCount}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the signs, let $b$ be a
sign, and let $x$ be a cube point. The number of coordinates at which $f$ is pivotal at
$x$ and $f(x)=b$, viewed as a real number, equals the sum over all coordinates of the
indicator that these two conditions hold.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of biased output pivotal probabilities]
\lean{FABL.sum_biasedOutputPivotalProbability}
\label{FABL.sum_biasedOutputPivotalProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign, FABL.biasedOutputPivotalProbability, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.outputPivotalCount, FABL.outputPivotalCount_cast, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_sum, FABL.productMean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, choose an output sign
$b\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $p\in(0,1)$. Give the coordinates of $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$
independent signs with probability $p$ of being $-1$. For each coordinate $i$, the
probability that $f(x)=b$ and flipping coordinate $i$ changes the value of $f$ is summed
over all $i$; this sum equals the expected number of coordinates with those two
properties.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence bound from negative pivotal count]
\lean{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_complement_mul_of_negOnePivotalCount_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b007
}
\label{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_complement_mul_of_negOnePivotalCount_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.outputPivotalCount, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono, FABL.productInfluence_eq_four_mul_complement_mul_negOnePivotalProbability_of_monotone, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productTotalInfluence, FABL.sum_biasedOutputPivotalProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\\in(0,1)$, let $f$ be a monotone sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign
cube, and let $w$ be a natural number. If at every input at most $w$ coordinates are
pivotal while the output is $-1$, then the total influence of $f$ under the product
distribution with bias parameter $p$ is at most $4(1-p)w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence bound from DNF width]
\lean{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_complement_mul_of_hasDNFWidthLE_of_monotone}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003
}
\label{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_complement_mul_of_hasDNFWidthLE_of_monotone}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.HasDNFWidthLE, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_width, FABL.productTotalInfluence, FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_complement_mul_of_negOnePivotalCount_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\\in(0,1)$, let $f$ be a monotone sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign
cube, and let $w$ be a natural number. If $f$ is represented by a disjunctive normal
form whose width is at most $w$, then its total influence under the product distribution
with bias parameter $p$ is at most $4(1-p)w$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be monotone. If $f$
is represented by a disjunctive normal form whose terms each contain at most $w$
distinct literals, where $w\in\mathbb N$, then under the product distribution on signs
with $\Pr[X_i=-1]=p$ independently for each coordinate, for any $0<p<1$, the total
product influence of $f$ is at most $4w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flipping commutes with global negation]
\lean{FABL.flipCoordinate_negateSignCube}
\label{FABL.flipCoordinate_negateSignCube}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
For every sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$ and coordinate $i$, flipping coordinate $i$ in
the globally negated vector $-x$ gives the global negation of the vector obtained by
flipping coordinate $i$ in $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Duality exchanges pivotal outputs]
\lean{FABL.isNegOnePivotal_booleanDual_negate_iff}
\label{FABL.isNegOnePivotal_booleanDual_negate_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.flipCoordinate_negateSignCube}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $x$ be a point of the
cube. The Boolean dual of $f$ is pivotal at coordinate $i$ with output $-1$ at the point
obtained by negating every coordinate of $x$ if and only if $f$ is pivotal at coordinate
$i$ with output $1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pivotal count bound from CNF width]
\lean{FABL.outputPivotalCount_one_le_of_hasCNFWidthLE}
\label{FABL.outputPivotalCount_one_le_of_hasCNFWidthLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.HasCNFWidthLE, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.IsOutputPivotal, FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_width, FABL.isNegOnePivotal_booleanDual_negate_iff, FABL.outputPivotalCount}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $w$ be a natural
number, and suppose $f$ is represented by a CNF formula of width at most $w$. At every
cube point, the number of coordinates where $f$ equals $1$ and is pivotal is at most
$w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence bound from positive pivotal count]
\lean{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_bias_mul_of_onePivotalCount_le}
\label{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_bias_mul_of_onePivotalCount_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.outputPivotalCount, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono, FABL.productInfluence_eq_four_mul_bias_mul_onePivotalProbability_of_monotone, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productTotalInfluence, FABL.sum_biasedOutputPivotalProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\\in(0,1)$, let $f$ be a monotone sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign
cube, and let $w$ be a natural number. If at every input at most $w$ coordinates are
pivotal while the output is $+1$, then the total influence of $f$ under the product
distribution with bias parameter $p$ is at most $4pw$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence bound from CNF width]
\lean{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_bias_mul_of_hasCNFWidthLE_of_monotone}
\label{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_bias_mul_of_hasCNFWidthLE_of_monotone}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let $p\\in(0,1)$, let $f$ be a monotone sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign
cube, and let $w$ be a natural number. If $f$ is represented by a conjunctive normal
form whose width is at most $w$, then its total influence under the product distribution
with bias parameter $p$ is at most $4pw$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence bound for monotone CNFs]
\lean{FABL.productTotalInfluence_le_four_mul_of_hasCNFWidthLE_of_monotone}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be monotone. If $f$
is represented by a conjunctive normal form whose clauses each contain at most $w$
distinct literals, where $w\in\mathbb N$, then under the product distribution on signs
with $\Pr[X_i=-1]=p$ independently for each coordinate, for any $0<p<1$, the total
product influence of $f$ is at most $4w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance of a biased Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.productVariance_biased_toReal_eq_four_mul_probability_mul_complement}
\label{FABL.productVariance_biased_toReal_eq_four_mul_probability_mul_complement}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasedMinusProbability, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_eq, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productMean, FABL.productMean_toReal_eq_one_sub_two_mul_minusProbability, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_toReal_eq_one_sub_sq_mean, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $0<p<1$. Write
$\widehat f(S)$ for the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and define
$q_f(p)=\frac{1-\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}(1-2p)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)}{2}$. Then the
variance of $f$ under the product distribution with $\Pr[X_i=-1]=p$ independently for
each coordinate is $4q_f(p)(1-q_f(p))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Interior range of the polynomial]
\lean{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo}
\label{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function
on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. For every $p$ with $0<p<1$, the biased-minus
probability polynomial of $f$ at $p$ lies strictly between $0$ and $1$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.thresholdSignMeasurableSpace}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p208-b005,

\proofstep
  {FABL.thresholdSignMeasurableSingletonClass}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p208-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p208-b006}
Let $f$ be a monotone Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let
$0<p<1$. The derivative of its biased-minus probability polynomial at $p$ is at least
the polynomial’s value at $p$ times one minus that value, divided by $p(1-p)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative lower bound below critical bias]
\lean{FABL.deriv_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge_div_two_mul}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b014}
\label{FABL.deriv_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge_div_two_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.deriv_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge_logistic, FABL.strictMonoOn_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube.
Suppose $p\text{ and }p_c$ are real numbers with $0<p<1$, $0\le p_c\le1$, and $p\le p_c$,
and the biased-minus probability polynomial of $f$ has value $1/2$ at $p_c$. Then its
derivative at $p$ is at least its value at $p$ divided by $2p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic derivative lower bound]
\lean{FABL.deriv_log_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b014}
\label{FABL.deriv_log_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.deriv_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge_div_two_mul, FABL.hasDerivAt_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_eq_totalInfluence, FABL.productTotalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube.
Suppose $p,p_c$ are real numbers with $0<p<1$, $0\le p_c\le1$, and $p\le p_c$, and the
biased-minus probability polynomial of $f$ has value $1/2$ at $p_c$. Then the derivative
at $p$ of the logarithm of that polynomial is at least $1/(2p)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Weak threshold logarithmic ratio]
\lean{FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio}
\label{FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and let $p$ be real.
The weak threshold logarithmic ratio is the natural logarithm of the biased-minus
probability polynomial of $f$ at $p$, minus one half the natural logarithm of $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the threshold log ratio]
\lean{FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio_monotoneOn}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b014}
\label{FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio_monotoneOn}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.continuous_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.deriv_log_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge, FABL.hasDerivAt_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_eq_totalInfluence, FABL.productTotalInfluence, FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone and nonconstant. Let $p_c\in(0,1)$ satisfy
that the biased minus probability polynomial of $f$ at $p_c$ equals $1/2$. Then the
function $p\mapsto\log Q_f(p)-\tfrac12\log p$, where $Q_f$ is that biased minus
probability polynomial, is monotone on $(0,p_c]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic bound at the critical parameter]
\lean{FABL.log_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_critical}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b014,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b015
}
\label{FABL.log_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_critical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio, FABL.weakThresholdLogRatio_monotoneOn}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone and nonconstant. For $p\in\mathbb R$, write
$Q_f(p)$ for the biased minus-probability polynomial of $f$. Suppose $0<p_0\le pc$,
$0<pc<1$, and $Q_f(pc)=1/2$. Then
\[
\log Q_f(p_0)-\frac12\log p_0\le \log\frac12-\frac12\log pc.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical square-root bound]
\lean{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_div_critical}
\label{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_div_critical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_endpoints, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.log_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_critical}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function
on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose $0<p_c<1$, $0\le p_0\le p_c$, and the
biased-minus probability polynomial of $f$ at $p_c$ equals $1/2$. Then its value at
$p_0$ is at most $\frac12\sqrt{p_0/p_c}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Small-parameter bound from a critical point]
\lean{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_epsilon_of_le_sq_mul_critical}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p238-b015}
\label{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_epsilon_of_le_sq_mul_critical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_div_critical}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube.
Suppose $\epsilon>0$, $0\le p_0\le p_c$, $p_c\in(0,1)$, the biased minus-probability
polynomial of $f$ at $p_c$ equals $1/2$, and $p_0\le(2\epsilon)^2p_c$. Then the
polynomial at $p_0$ is at most $\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative bound for the negative log complement]
\lean{FABL.deriv_neg_log_one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge}
\label{FABL.deriv_neg_log_one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.biasSigma, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.deriv_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge_logistic, FABL.hasDerivAt_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_eq_totalInfluence, FABL.productTotalInfluence, FABL.strictMonoOn_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube.
Suppose $p_c,p$ are real numbers with $0<p_c<1$, $0<p<1$, and $p_c\le p$, and the
biased-minus probability polynomial of $f$ has value $1/2$ at $p_c$. Then the derivative
at $p$ of the negative logarithm of one minus that polynomial is at least $1/(2p)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Weak upper-threshold logarithmic ratio]
\lean{FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio}
\label{FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial}
For a Boolean function $f$ on $
\{−1,1\}^n$ and a real number $p$, let $q_f(p)$ denote its biased-minus probability
polynomial. The weak upper-threshold logarithmic ratio is $-\log(1-q_f(p)) -
\tfrac12\log p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the threshold log ratio]
\lean{FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio_monotoneOn}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p239-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p239-b002
}
\label{FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio_monotoneOn}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.continuous_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.deriv_neg_log_one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_ge, FABL.hasDerivAt_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_eq_totalInfluence, FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on
the $n$-dimensional sign cube, taking values in $\{-1,1\}$. Let $p_c\in(0,1/2)$ and
suppose the biased minus-probability polynomial of $f$ at $p_c$ equals $1/2$. Then the
function $p\mapsto-\log(1-q_f(p))-\tfrac12\log p$, where $q_f$ is that biased
minus-probability polynomial, is monotone on $[p_c,1/2]$; that is, it is nondecreasing
there.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Square-root bound for biased probability]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_critical_div}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p239-b001}
\label{FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_critical_div}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_mem_Ioo, FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio, FABL.weakUpperThresholdLogRatio_monotoneOn}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function. For
$S\\subseteq[n]$, write $\\widehat f(S)=\\mathbb E_x[f(x)\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i]$ for its
uniform Fourier coefficient, and set
$P_f(q)=\\bigl(1-\\sum_{S\\subseteq[n]}(1-2q)^{|S|}\\widehat f(S)\\bigr)/2$. If
$0<p_c<1/2$, $p_c\\le p\\le1/2$, and $P_f(p_c)=1/2$, then
$1-P_f(p)\\le\\frac12\\sqrt{p_c/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Biased minus probability bound]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_epsilon}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p239-b001}
\label{FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_epsilon}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_critical_div}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function. For
$S\\subseteq[n]$, write $\\widehat f(S)=\\mathbb E_x[f(x)\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i]$ for its
uniform Fourier coefficient, and set
$P_f(q)=\\bigl(1-\\sum_{S\\subseteq[n]}(1-2q)^{|S|}\\widehat f(S)\\bigr)/2$. Suppose
$\\epsilon>0$, $0<p_c<1/2$, $p_c\\le p\\le1/2$, $P_f(p_c)=1/2$, and
$p_c/(2\\epsilon)^2\\le p$. Then $1-P_f(p)\\le\\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Square-root bound at half bias]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_one_half_le_sqrt_critical_div_two}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p239-b001}
\label{FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_one_half_le_sqrt_critical_div_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.one_sub_biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_le_half_mul_sqrt_critical_div}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function. For
$S\\subseteq[n]$, write $\\widehat f(S)=\\mathbb E_x[f(x)\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i]$ for its
uniform Fourier coefficient, and set
$P_f(q)=\\bigl(1-\\sum_{S\\subseteq[n]}(1-2q)^{|S|}\\widehat f(S)\\bigr)/2$. If
$0<p_c<1/2$ and $P_f(p_c)=1/2$, then $1-P_f(1/2)\\le\\sqrt{p_c/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Biased sign average]
\lean{FABL.biasedSignAverage}
\label{FABL.biasedSignAverage}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue}
For a positive integer $n$ and $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, the biased sign average is the sum of
the sign values of the coordinates of $x$, divided by $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product biased-sign measure]
\lean{FABL.productProbabilityPMF_biasedSign_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\label{FABL.productProbabilityPMF_biasedSign_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF_toMeasure, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p\in[0,1]$. On the sign set $\{-1,1\}$, take
the probability law that assigns probability $p$ to $-1$ and probability $1-p$ to $1$.
The measure associated with its $n$-fold independent product distribution equals the
product measure whose coordinate marginals are this same sign law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Concentration of the biased sign average]
\lean{FABL.measure_abs_biasedSignAverage_sub_mean_ge_le}
\label{FABL.measure_abs_biasedSignAverage_sub_mean_ge_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.biasMean, FABL.biasedSignAverage, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF_signValue, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_integral, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productProbabilityPMF_biasedSign_toMeasure_eq_pi, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $t\ge0$. Choose $n$ independent
signs $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\{-1,1\}$, each equal to $1$ with probability $1-p$ and to $-1$
with probability $p$, and write $A_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$. Then $\Pr(|A_n-(1-2p)|\ge
t)\le 2\exp(-nt^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Negative average under negative odd majority]
\lean{FABL.biasedSignAverage_neg_of_majority_odd_eq_neg_one}
\label{FABL.biasedSignAverage_neg_of_majority_odd_eq_neg_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedSignAverage, FABL.majority, FABL.signValue, FABL.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$ and every sign vector $x$ of length $2m+1$, if the majority
of its coordinates is $-1$, then the average of its coordinates is strictly negative.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.biasedSignAverage_neg_of_majority_odd_eq_neg_one}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p043-b004}
For every integer $m\ge 0$ and real $C\ge 0$ such that $C/\sqrt{2m+1}\le 1/2$, let $X$
be a uniformly independent sign vector of length $2m+1$ whose coordinates equal $-1$
with probability $p=1/2-C/\sqrt{2m+1}$. The probability that the majority of the
coordinates is $-1$ is at most $2\exp(-2C^2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative average under positive odd majority]
\lean{FABL.biasedSignAverage_nonneg_of_majority_odd_eq_one}
\label{FABL.biasedSignAverage_nonneg_of_majority_odd_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedSignAverage, FABL.majority, FABL.signValue, FABL.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$ and every sign vector $x$ of length $2m+1$, if the majority
of its coordinates is $1$, then the average of its coordinates is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability as event measure]
\lean{FABL.biasedMinusProbability_eq_measureReal}
\label{FABL.biasedMinusProbability_eq_measureReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.biasedMinusProbability, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_integral, FABL.productMean, FABL.productProbabilityPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, and suppose $p\in[0,1]$. Under the product probability distribution on the
sign cube with coordinate bias determined by $p$, the biased-minus probability of $f$
equals the probability of the event that $f$ takes the value $-1$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.biasedMinusProbability_eq_measureReal}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p221-b002}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C\geq0$ satisfy $C/\sqrt{2m+1}\leq\frac12$.
For independent signs, each equal to $-1$ with probability $p=\frac12+C/\sqrt{2m+1}$ and
to $1$ otherwise, the probability that their majority is $-1$ is at least
$1-2\exp(-2C^2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Condorcet constant]
\lean{FABL.condorcetConstant}
\label{FABL.condorcetConstant}
\leanok
For a real number $\epsilon$, the Condorcet constant is
$\sqrt{\max\{0,\tfrac12\log(2/\epsilon)\}}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the Condorcet constant]
\lean{FABL.condorcetConstant_nonneg}
\label{FABL.condorcetConstant_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.condorcetConstant}
\difficulty{1}
For every real number $\epsilon$, the Condorcet constant
$\sqrt{\max\{0,\log(2/\epsilon)/2\}}$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential bound for the Condorcet constant]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_exp_neg_two_mul_condorcetConstant_sq_le}
\label{FABL.two_mul_exp_neg_two_mul_condorcetConstant_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.condorcetConstant}
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $\epsilon>0$, let $c=\sqrt{\max\bigl(0,\log(2/\epsilon)/2\bigr)}$.
Then $2\exp(-2c^2)\leq\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Threshold bounds for majority]
\lean{FABL.exists_condorcetMajorityThresholdBounds}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p225-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b008
}
\label{FABL.exists_condorcetMajorityThresholdBounds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial, FABL.biasedMinusProbabilityPolynomial_eq, FABL.biasedMinusProbability_majority_lower_le_two_mul_exp, FABL.condorcetConstant, FABL.condorcetConstant_nonneg, FABL.majority, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_exp_le_biasedMinusProbability_majority_upper, FABL.two_mul_exp_neg_two_mul_condorcetConstant_sq_le}
\difficulty{4}
\proofstep
  {FABL.𝔽₂}

  {FABL.condorcetConstant}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p225-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b008}

  {FABL.condorcetConstant_nonneg}
